parameters.name: outcome
parameters.notes: **One of four, each meaning something different to the books** (BR-3): sold brings money in and needs a receipt and a ledger entry; scrapped brings nothing; donated brings nothing but is recorded; lost is a write-off and, in the document's own words, probably an investigation (BR-11). Never collapsed into one word and never guessed.

parameters.name: proceeds
parameters.notes: The amount received. **Required where the outcome is sold** (E3) and refused on the other three — nothing comes in on a scrapping, a donation or a loss (BR-3, BR-5, E10).

parameters.name: donated_to
parameters.notes: Who the asset was donated to. Required where the outcome is donated (E4) — recorded even though nothing comes in (BR-3).

fields.name: status

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: Sold, scrapped, donated or lost (BR-3).

fields.name: is_write_off
fields.description: True where the outcome is lost. Flagged as such, since it is the outcome that most often needs looking into rather than merely recording — and **nothing follows the flag** (BR-11, OQ-2).

fields.name: purchase_value
fields.description: What the asset cost, from the voucher on the register (UC-18-07 BR-3).

fields.name: total_maintenance_cost
fields.description: What it has already cost to keep. The approver sees this before deciding — a disposal judged without it is a decision made blind (BR-8, UC-18-09 BR-6).

fields.name: remaining_book_value
fields.description: **None.** Nothing in the system calculates depreciation, so no asset carries one — and the gain or loss cannot be computed without it (BR-4, E7, OQ-1).

fields.name: approver_required
fields.description: Derived from the asset's value and the thresholds the Super Admin set, following the voucher thresholds. Never chosen — and the thresholds themselves are not stated anywhere (BR-2, OQ-3).

fields.name: still_assigned_to
fields.description: Who or what holds it. The disposal ends the assignment when it completes, not now (BR-7).

errors.meaning: The asset has already been disposed of.
The outcome is sold and no proceeds were entered.
The outcome is donated and no recipient was recorded.
Proceeds were recorded for a scrapped, donated or lost asset.
errors.note: Nothing comes in on those outcomes, and each produces a loss equal to the whole remaining book value (BR-3, BR-5).

planningRules.rule: Never choose the outcome. Sold, scrapped, donated and lost are four different facts about where a school's property went, and collapsing them is exactly what the rule forbids — a lost asset recorded as scrapped is a loss nobody will ever look into (BR-3, BR-11).

Give the maintenance total and the purchase value before anything is decided. A disposal judged without knowing what has already been spent on the thing is a decision made blind, and that is the reason the history is kept at all (BR-8, BR-5 of UC-18-09).
Say that raising retires nothing. The asset stays on the register, still assigned to whoever has it, until the disposal is approved and completed (BR-2, BR-6, BR-7, E6).
Say plainly that a loss is flagged and nothing follows the flag. The document calls it probably an investigation, and no process anywhere follows (BR-11, OQ-2).

Say that no asset carries a remaining book value. Nothing calculates depreciation anywhere in the system, so the gain or loss this use case exists to post cannot be computed — the disposal will not complete (BR-4, E7, OQ-1).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A disposal awaiting approval is returned with a reason and the asset stays on the register — nothing has happened to it. A disposal raised and returned stays on the record, and neither the disposal nor the asset is ever deleted (BR-10, E9).

planningRules.rule: Say before anything else that this cannot complete. No asset in the system carries a remaining book value because nothing calculates depreciation, and the gain or loss has nothing to be measured against — the use case says so itself (BR-4, E7, OQ-1). It is a gap in the specification, not a fault to work around.
Never invent a book value to make the arithmetic work. A figure nobody computed, posted to the ledger as a gain or a loss, is worse than a disposal that did not complete (BR-4).
Say what the outcome does to the books. A sale nets proceeds against book value; a scrapping, a donation and a loss each write off the whole of it, because nothing comes in (BR-3, BR-5).
Say that the assignment ends here. The asset comes off whoever's holdings and off every exit handover checklist at the moment of completion, and not when the disposal was approved (BR-7).
Say that nothing is deleted. The asset leaves the register and its purchase, assignments, maintenance and verifications stay readable — a disposed asset is still answerable for (BR-6, BR-10, E9).
Say that the buyer is nowhere. On a sale the proceeds are recorded and who paid them is not, which the specification raises and does not settle (OQ-4).

planningRules.rule: Never collapse the four outcomes. Sold, scrapped, donated and lost are different facts about where school property went, and only one of them means somebody should be asking questions (BR-3, BR-11).

Name the disposals approved and not completed, and say why. In practice that is all of them: no asset carries a remaining book value, so nothing can be posted — those assets are approved for retirement and still on the register, still counted, still assigned (BR-4, E7, OQ-1).
List the assets written off as lost with their values, and say that nothing follows. Each is flagged and no process anywhere picks up the flag (BR-11, OQ-2).
Say that the proceeds have no buyer against them. What was received is recorded and who paid it is not (OQ-4).
Say that a disposed asset stays on the register. Nothing is deleted, so a total taken off the register includes equipment that has already gone (BR-6, BR-10).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing. The record it reads is never deleted (BR-10, E9).

request.text: is saal kaunse assets retire hue hain aur kitna paisa aaya?
request.gloss: which assets were retired this year and how much came in?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give it split four ways — sold, scrapped, donated, lost — never as one figure. Then the answer that matters more than the totals: **nothing has actually been retired.** Every approved disposal is stuck at completion, because the gain or loss needs a remaining book value and no asset in this system has one. All of them are still on the register, still counted in its value, and several still assigned to people.

request.text: kitni cheezein gum shuda likhi gayi hain?
request.gloss: how many things have been written off as lost?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give each with its purchase value and the total. Say plainly that every one is flagged as a write-off and that nothing in the system does anything with the flag — the specification calls a loss probably an investigation and no process follows it. If anybody is to look into these, a person has to decide that.
